title: Max Chunks To Make Sorted II
description:
# Max Chunks To Make Sorted II

You are given an integer array `arr`, which may contain duplicate values.

Split `arr` into one or more non-empty contiguous chunks. Sort each chunk independently, then concatenate the sorted chunks in their original order. The final concatenated array must equal `arr` sorted as one whole array.

Return the largest possible number of chunks.

## Example 1

**Input:** arr = [5,4,3,2,1]

**Output:** 1

**Explanation:** Any split into two or more chunks keeps at least one large value before a smaller value after concatenation. The whole array must stay as one chunk.

## Example 2

**Input:** arr = [2,1,3,4,4]

**Output:** 4

**Explanation:** One optimal split is `[2,1] | [3] | [4] | [4]`. Sorting each chunk gives `[1,2] | [3] | [4] | [4]`, which concatenates to `[1,2,3,4,4]`.

## Constraints

* `1 <= arr.length <= 2000`
* `0 <= arr[i] <= 10^8`

solutions.name: Monotonic Stack of Chunk Maximums
solutions.description:
## Approach

Maintain a stack where each entry is the maximum value of one currently valid chunk. When the next value is at least the top chunk maximum, it can start a new chunk. Otherwise, every previous chunk whose maximum is greater than this value must merge with the current value; keep the largest maximum of that merged block and push it back.

## Key Insight

A boundary is invalid as soon as a later value is smaller than a chunk maximum on the left. The monotonic stack stores exactly the chunk maxima that have survived so far, and popping merges all chunks that the new value proves incompatible.

## Complexity Analysis

Each element is pushed once and popped at most once, so the time complexity is O(n). The stack can contain at most n chunk maxima, giving O(n) space.

solutions.name: Prefix Max with Suffix Min
solutions.description:
## Approach

Precompute `suffixMin[i]`, the minimum value in `arr[i..n-1]`. Scan left to right while maintaining the maximum value in the current prefix. A boundary after index `i` is valid exactly when the largest value on the left is no greater than the smallest value on the right.

## Key Insight

If `max(left) <= min(right)`, then after sorting the left chunk and the remaining right-side chunks, no left value needs to move past a right value. If the inequality fails, some larger left value must cross the boundary, so the boundary cannot be kept.

## Complexity Analysis

The suffix minimum array and the final scan are both linear. Time complexity is O(n), and the suffix array uses O(n) space.

solutions.name: Sorted Prefix Sum Equality
solutions.description:
## Approach

Sort a copy of `arr`. Scan both arrays in parallel and compare the prefix sums. Whenever the original prefix sum equals the sorted prefix sum, the original prefix contains exactly the multiset of values that belong before this boundary, so a chunk can end here.

## Key Insight

The constraint `arr[i] >= 0` matters: for any fixed prefix length, the sorted prefix has the minimum possible sum among all prefixes of that length. Equality means the original prefix did not include any value outside that smallest multiset, except for equal duplicate values.

## Complexity Analysis

Sorting takes O(n log n), and the scan is O(n). The sorted copy uses O(n) space.

solutions.name: Sorted Prefix Multiset Balance
solutions.description:
## Approach

Sort a copy of the array. While scanning index `i`, add `arr[i]` to a difference map and subtract `sorted[i]` from the same map. Track how many values currently have a nonzero difference. A boundary is valid exactly when all differences return to zero.

## Key Insight

A chunk boundary means the original prefix and the sorted prefix contain the same multiset, not merely the same maximum. The difference map states that condition directly and handles duplicates without relying on a numeric shortcut.

## Complexity Analysis

Sorting costs O(n log n). Each map adjustment is expected O(1), so the scan is O(n). The map and sorted copy use O(n) space.

solutions.name: Stable Sorted Rank Mapping
solutions.description:
## Approach

Sort a copy of `arr` and assign every occurrence in the sorted array a stable target index. Use queues per value so duplicates receive distinct target positions. Then scan the original array, map each value to its next target index, and cut whenever the maximum target index seen so far equals the current index.

## Key Insight

After stable ranking, the problem becomes the permutation version: a prefix can be a chunk exactly when all ranked positions needed by that prefix are also inside the prefix. The condition `maxRank == i` captures that closure.

## Complexity Analysis

Sorting takes O(n log n). Building queues and scanning the original array are O(n). The queues store n target indices, so the extra space is O(n).
